claims.text: The untreated (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a robust caloric response.
The untreated alloy has poor mechanical integrity and a propensity to crack.
The cracking propensity is caused by the alloy's brittle nature.
Post-homogenization aging at 500–600 °C for 1–4 hours will induce fine-scale nano-precipitates.
The aging treatment can produce precipitates that are coherent with the parent matrix.
The aging-induced nano-precipitates will be ductile.
The nano-precipitates will be distributed both along grain boundaries and within grains.
The nano-precipitates will act as barriers to crack propagation.
Ductile nano-precipitates will blunt crack tips.
Blocking crack-propagation routes will enhance mechanical toughness.
Crystallographic coherence of the precipitates will preserve the magnetostructural transition.
The magnetostructural transition underpins the alloy's caloric response.
The heat-treated alloy will have a compressive strength above 220 MPa.
The heat-treated alloy will maintain a caloric entropy change similar to that of the untreated alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will maintain magnetostructural-transition sharpness similar to that of the untreated alloy.
The proposed benefits are expected under applied magnetic fields, pressure fields, temperatures near the magnetostructural transition, and compressive loading.
Precipitate coarsening could degrade mechanical toughness or caloric performance.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires compressive strength above 220 MPa, but the falsification rule only rejects the hypothesis when strength fails to improve significantly over the control. A significant increase that remains below 220 MPa would violate the quantitative prediction without meeting the stated falsification criterion.
